claims.claim: 'Ego et dominus meus Sophronius perrezimns ad philosophi Stephani domum, docirinæ gralia ; ; erat autem meridianum tempus'; the girl: 'Dorwit iſle , oporiet exspectare pusillum'; 'Tune aio domino meo Sophronio: Eamus ad Tetra- pylum'; 'neminem invenimus nisi ec0s tres' (the three blind men); the third: 'Tune resedit coram me mortyus, extendensque super me manus Suas, digitis suis eruit oculos meos'; 'innuit mihi }1»winus meus Sopbronius, et recessimus. Et dixit mihi: Vere, abba Joannes, hodie nibil ultra studea- mus; satis enim edificati sumus' (OCR as in the file: 'Tune' = Tunc, 'perrezimns' = perreximus, 'Dorwit iſle' = Dormit ille, 'ec0s' = eos, 'mortyus', '}1»winus' = dominus); the brief tells it in modern words, the closing words as a modern rendering of the Latin
claims.witness: John Moschus, Spiritual Meadow ch. 77, Latin column (john-moschus pg87-3 l.9983-9993, 10006-10007, 10086-10095)

claims.claim: The third blind man had followed the funeral of a dead man 'optime indutum' and, entering the tomb, 'exui ipsum, nihil ei relinquens preter unum lintes- men'
claims.witness: Spiritual Meadow ch. 77 (john-moschus pg87-3 l.10053-10058)

claims.claim: Dedication 'JOANNIS EVIRATUS DILECTO suo IN CHRISTO, SOPHRONIO SOPHISTR.'; 'Ex his ego flores pucherrimos decerpens, coronam tibi ex immarcescibili ac perenni prato contexui, fidelis- sime fili, eamque libi, ac per te omnibus offero' (OCR 'SOPHISTR.' = SOPHISTAE, 'pucherrimos', 'libi' = tibi); the closing line is a modern rendering of the Latin
claims.witness: Spiritual Meadow, dedication, Latin column (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3756-3757, 3781-3786)

claims.claim: The old notice: 'Primi porro auctoris elogium (quod bona ex parte Photius Bibliothecæ suæ inservit, integreque ex MS. codice Vaticano antiquo a Francisco Oli- varii Latine redditum, Heribertus noster Roswey- dus edidit inter vitas Patrum)'; later called 'prefixum Prato spirituali elogium'
claims.witness: Daniel Papebroch, Life of Sophronius (Acta Sanctorum, March II, p. 65, reprinted by Migne) (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24917-24921, 25462-25463); the Life is Papebroch's by Fabricius's notice, 'Papebrochius in Actis Sanctor. ad 11 Martii tom. II, p. 65 seq.' (l.3521-3522) and Migne's heading (l.24641)

claims.claim: The notice: he renounced the world 'in monasterio saneti Patris nostri Theo- dosii, abbatis et archimandritz omnium, que sunt Hierosolymis, cenobiorum'; lived 'in deserto ad sanctum Jordanem non exiguo tempore'; then 'in Novo, quod dicitur, manasterio, quod a sancto et magno Palre nostro Saba ejusque discipulis eon- structum'; 'audiens qua tyrannide Persæ Romanos oppressissent, oc- casione cedis Mauritii imperatoris ejusque liberorum ... perrexit ad par- tes Antiochiz magne'; then 'Alexandriam se contulit' and went 'nsque ad Oasim'; hearing 'saneta loca fuisse occupata', 'ad magnam Romanorum urbem navigio appulit una cum cha- rissimo diseipulo suo Sopbronio'
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24932-24965); an anonymous notice of unknown date

claims.claim: The notice: he wrote the book 'cum (sun ad Deum migrationis tempus previdis- set'; handed it to Sophronius; asked 'ui reliquias suas ne Rome relinqueret, sed area lignea inclusas ad montem Sinzum transſerre co- naretur', or, if a barbarian tumult prevented it, 'in monasterio 8. Theo- dosii ... ipsas deponi'; at Ascalon the way to Sinai was barred 'propter tyrannicas incur- siones eorum, qui yocantur Agareni'; at Jerusalem 'in S. Theodosii cœmeterio deposuit' (OCR 'sun' = suae, 'area' = arca, 'Sinzum' = Sinaeum)
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25365-25398, 25455-25462)

claims.claim: Papebroch: 'Annum revergionis significat octave indi- clionis character vi cesimum supra $excentesimum ſuisse' (620; OCR 'revergionis')
claims.witness: Papebroch (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25355, 25403-25405, column break between 'indi-' and 'clionis')

claims.claim: Papebroch: Tiberius began to reign 'anno 579 exeunte'; Maurice was killed 'circa finem anni 602'; Moschus reached Rome 'In exitnu erat papz Deus-dedit pontificatus, vel Bonifacii Vinchoatus'
claims.witness: Papebroch (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24979-24984, 25324-25326)

claims.claim: Papebroch: the book was first spread by Sophronius, who had brought it 'a magistro Ro- me, ubi perſectus demum est, moriente, velut testamento acceptum, una cum deſuncti cadavere in Palæstinam'
claims.witness: Papebroch (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24815-24820)

claims.claim: Fabricius: monastic life 'in conobio 8. Theodosii (e), Hierosolymis et in deserto ad Jordanem et in nova S. Sabe laura'; 'notissimumque illum librum de Vitis monachorum illius etatis usque ad Heraelii 4 tempora fabulosis non destitutum narrationibus, composuit ad Sophronium sophistam, discipulum (/) et itinerum comitem, (deinde patriarcham Hierosolymitanum)'; 'Passim ... invehitur in heresin Severi Acephali'; 'Diem obiisse supremuin a. C. 620, a Joanne Bollando adnotatum reperi'
claims.witness: Notice from Fabricius, Bibliotheca Graeca, ed. Harles, l. X, p. 124, as Migne prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3368-3400; OCR rough). The notice mixes Fabricius's text with Harles's additions (marked 'HAL.'); the sentences cited stand in its first paragraph, before any 'HAL.' mark

claims.claim: Severus is Severus of Antioch, who rejected Chalcedon: 'Severus sedem Antiochenam expulso S. Fla- ano per vim invasit anno 513, ex secta Acepha- lorum'; Severus wrote 'adversus Joannem Cæsa- riensem Grammaticum concilii Chalcedonensis de- ſensorem'
claims.witness: Notes in the same volume (john-moschus pg87-3 l.37983-37985, 5774-5776)

claims.claim: Second Council of Nicaea: 'Stephanus itaque monachus acceptum librum legit : « Ejusdem Pairis nostri Sophronii e Limonario; dixit Theodorus abbas, Xliotes, quod erat quidam inclusus (b); » et cztera. Ubi totum caput 45, quod in hoc libro babetur, ad verbum redditur'; John of Damascus and the synod 'librum Sophronio patriarchæ Hierosolymitano inscribunt'
claims.witness: Aloysius Lipomanus, letter to the reader (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3664-3672)

claims.claim: The year of Nicaea II: 'In Actis synodi septime, sive Nicene secundo (a. C. 787 manu aliquoties laudatur Sophronius. afferunturque loca sub illius nomine' (OCR as in the file)
claims.witness: Notice on Sophronius in the same volume, after 'Hactenus Fabricius' (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24447-24449); whose words (Fabricius's or Harles's) the section is is not marked

claims.claim: Chapter 45: an 'inclusus in monte Olivarum'; the demon: 'Noli adorare bane ima- ginem, et ultra te non impugaabo'; the image 'expres:am ſiguram dominæ nostrę sanctz Dei genitricis Marie, ſerentem Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum'; Theodore: 'Expedit au- tem bi nullum in illa urbe lupanar omitiere, quod non ingrediaris, quam ut neges ie adorare Deum, et Dominum nostrum Jesum Christuin cum matre sua'
claims.witness: Spiritual Meadow ch. 45 (john-moschus pg87-3 l.7564-7590)

claims.claim: Lipomanus: the writer was John (ch. 77); 'Pho- uus quoque hune ipsum auctorem libri Joannem Moschum (natione fortasse) ſuisse asserit, cujus coguo- men interpres Latinus forsan Eviratum reddidit'; the book is given to Sophronius because it is addressed to him, because he takes part throughout, or because 'uns cum Joanne prædieto conscriptor (ut ita dicam) forte ejusdem libri fuit' (OCR 'uns' = una)
claims.witness: Lipomanus (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3675-3681, 3694-3695)

claims.claim: Lipomanus: 'Quo autem tempore viri hi, qui librum conscripserunt, claruerint, pro certo non habetur'; 'conjeclura aszequi possumus, circa annum Domini sexcentesimum, illum ſuisse conseriptum'
claims.witness: Lipomanus (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3711-3717)

claims.claim: Lipomanus: the book had been printed 'non nisi vernacula, atque en halica lingua'; it is so full of flowers 'ut in Paradisi deliciis ortus esse videatur'; John the Deacon in his Life of Gregory translated 'ex Gracorum relationibus' the story 'Enarravit nobis abbas Joannes Persa'
claims.witness: Lipomanus (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3613-3619, 3657-3663)

claims.claim: Lipomanus's Latin edition, Venice 1558: 'in tomo septimo Aloysii I. i- manni, Venet. 1558' (OCR 'I. i- manni' = Lipomanni)
claims.witness: Fabricius's notice (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3494-3496)

claims.claim: Chapter count: 'hodie autem solum novemdecim supra ducenta capita numerantur' against Photius's 'in quibusdam ad duo et quadraginta su- pra trecentas sese extendant'
claims.witness: Papebroch, quoting Photius (john-moschus pg87-3 l.25316-25321)

claims.claim: Nicephorus gives the book to Sophronius: 'Locupletem quoque et utilem de eis (monachis) Ri- sforiam Sophronius Hierosolymitanus nobis reliquit, Prati et novi Paradisi titulo'
claims.witness: Fabricius's notice, quoting Nicephorus VIII.41 (john-moschus pg87-3 l.3516-3520); 'Nicephorus Callistus' by name at l.25418

claims.claim: Names: 'BEATI JOANNIS EUCRATA LIBER QUI INSCRIBITUR PRATUM' (Migne's Latin heading of the Greek title); 'JOANNIS EVIRATUS' (dedication heading)
claims.witness: john-moschus pg87-3 l.3600-3606, 3756

claims.claim: The notice calls him 'Joanne sancte memorize presbytero, et monacho cogno- mento Moscho' (OCR 'memorize' = memoriae)
claims.witness: The old notice, as Papebroch prints it (john-moschus pg87-3 l.24932-24934)

claims.claim: Moschus a monk of Palestine: of St Theodosius, the Jordan desert and the New Laura of St Sabas
claims.witness: Fabricius (l.3378-3379) and the old notice (l.24932-24946), john-moschus pg87-3

contested_claims.sides: John of Damascus and the Second Council of Nicaea cite it as Sophronius's (Lipomanus, pg87-3 l.3664-3672; Papebroch l.24679-24697); Nicephorus gives it to Sophronius (Fabricius l.3516-3520). Lipomanus answers that the writer was John (ch. 77) and Photius names Moschus (l.3675-3678); Fabricius and Papebroch follow Photius and the dedication (l.3382-3386, 24679-24681); Papebroch explains the attribution by Sophronius's publishing it (l.24815-24820).

Fabricius reports 620 from John Bolland (l.3400); Papebroch reckons the return of the body to Palestine in the eighth indiction, 620 (l.25403-25405); Lipomanus says the time is not certain and guesses the book about 600 (l.3711-3717). No ancient line gives a year.

absent_details.detail: Photius's notice of the Meadow (Bibliotheca, codex 199)
absent_details.note: Not held. Freese's English Photius (photius_library-v1_freese1920.txt) is volume 1 only and has no entry naming Moschus, Eucrata, the Meadow or Sophronius's Leimon (searched). Known through Papebroch (l.24917-24921, 25316-25321), Lipomanus (l.3675-3678) and Fabricius's notes (l.3412-3416, OCR rough).

absent_details.detail: An English translation of the Meadow
absent_details.note: None held. Whole-Library search for Moschus/Moschi/Moscho, Eucrat-, Evirat-, Limonar-, Leimon, 'Spiritual Meadow' and 'Pratum spirituale' finds only citations (e.g. Wardrop's Life of Nino l.16933-17002, PO 8, PO 16, Acta Sanctorum March III); the file header says no public-domain English exists.
No held source gives them. The Library header's 'c. 550-619' rests on no held line.
The Greek column is garbled OCR; the brief and card follow the Latin column.

absent_details.detail: Who wrote the old notice and when
absent_details.note: Papebroch names no author or date; it came to Rosweyde in Olivarius's Latin from an old Vatican manuscript (l.24917-24921).

claims.claim: 'Un jour qu'il etait k lire i\ rhopital, le sommeil le prit. II entendit une voix terrible qui lui ordonnait d'emigrer au mont Izla aupres de Mar Abraham chef des moines'; 'U distribua ses biens ; et de tout ce que son pere lui avait laisse nayant pris avec lui que soixante stateres d'or pour les partager entre les moines' (OCR 'k lire i\ rhopital' = a lire a l'hopital, 'U' = Il)
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV, tr. Scher (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29640-29644); a later Arabic history, admiring

claims.claim: 'Ce Saint etait un des notables habitants de Zabdai ; il avait les avantages de la fortune, beaucoup de biens et d'esclaves'; studied Persian books, then medicine at the hospital of Nisibis and church learning at the School, 'quinze aus'; 'Depuis quil se fit moine, il ne coucha jamais sur une natte'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29611-29613, 29638-29639, 29646)

claims.claim: Thomas: 'this blessed man Mar Babhai came from Beth *Ainatha, a city of Beth Zabhdai'; 'a disciple of Mar Abraham. [And although he was] a learned and a wise man, he was by nature somewhat hasty of speech and harsh in command'; 'Mar Babhai had become the head of the community, being the third head in the order of succession'
claims.witness: Thomas of Marga, Book of Governors I.7, tr. Budge (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.2059-2060, 2100-2107); Thomas writes about 840 (Budge's title, l.94)

claims.claim: Dadisho succeeded Abraham, then Babai: 'Apr6s la mort de Rabban Mar Abraham -, son disciple Dadiso' lui succeda. Apres lui Babai fut ^Iu pour dirigcr le couvent'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29652-29653)

claims.claim: Jacob was driven out 'by the order and decree of the word of Mar Babhai'; the fathers 'rebuked and chid the head of the monastery'; Thomas omits the ban: 'I do not set it down here out of respect for Mar Babhai'; the dispersion: 'many of the holy fathers of that monastery were scattered abroad'; 'they filled the country of the East with monasteries'
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.12-14 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.2681-2683, 2759-2760, 2769-2770, 2938-2939, 3022); Thomas writes from Beth Abe, 'this our convent of Beth 'Abhe' (l.4309)

claims.claim: After the death of the catholicos Gregory, 'par la volonte de Kosrau Parwez, rEglise etant restee sans chef'; Babai, 'encourage par plusieurs metropolitains et eveques', worked to restore the church; 'Mar Habai nouvcrnu le couvent pcndant vingt-quatre ans. II mourut k Tage de soixante-quinze ans, en la trente- huitierae ann^e de Kosrau'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29657-29661, 29675-29680; OCR 'Habai nouvcrnu' = Babai gouverna)

claims.claim: Three metropolitans, 'Mar Cyriacus of Nisibis, Mar Yonadhabh of Adiabene, and Mar Gabriel of Karkha dhe Beth Slokh' (footnote marks in the file omitted here and below), persuaded Babai, 'a solitary and not a bishop', to 'visit the monasteries, and convents, and monks ... and drive out and expel from the Church him that was sick and broken in wickedness'; he served 'until the murder of the wicked King Khusrau'
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.27 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.4085-4140)

claims.claim: Chabot: during the vacancy 'l'Église fut dirigée par l'archidiacre Mar Aba et le célèbre archimandrite Babai l'An- cien'; Chosroes opposed the election of a new patriarch until 628
claims.witness: Chabot, appendix (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.37350-37361)

claims.claim: In 612 'Mar Babai, qui n'avait pas pu se rendre k cctte reunion k cause de sa faiblesse et de son kge avance, leur avait ete dun grand secours par sa plume'; he wrote 'un ouvrage, pour refuter le commentaire de Ilnana sur la doctrine des 318'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXXIII (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29556-29561); 612 is Scher's note ('En 612', l.29565)

claims.claim: Babai's Life of George: a monk calls Henana 'cet homme qui enseigne le fatalisme' who 'nie la résurrection des corps'; Babai names him 'Henana l'hérétique, le chal- déen et lorigéniste'
claims.witness: Babai, Life of George, extracts tr. Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42081-42083, 42093-42104, 42110-42112); consistent with henana-of-adiabene (batch 5)

claims.claim: The charges against Henana rest on Babai; Braun: 'der leidenschaftliche Babai von Jzala', with 'Uebertreibungen und Widersprüche'
claims.witness: Braun (synodicon-orientale braun1900 l.13690-13696); batch 5 records for henana-of-adiabene

claims.claim: Book of the Union quoted by Labourt from an unpublished copy: 'Grâce à l'obligeance de M. Chabot, nous sommes en mesure d'adjoindre à ces textes un traité inédit de Babaï sur l'Incarnation (De unione)'; 'quand nous parlons de cette union [de l'Incarnation], nous disons : Le Christ est mort, le Fils est mort, par le Fils tout a été créé et fait, bien que nous comprenions que tels attributs appartiennent à l'hu- manité qui a reçu la mort, et tels autres à la divinité par qui tout a été créé et fait'; 'en sorte qu'il n'y a pas deux Fils ou deux Fils du Très-Haut'; the brief's quotation is a modern English rendering of Labourt's French
claims.witness: Babai, Book of the Union, in Labourt's French (labourt1904 l.15763-15768, 15845-15866)

claims.claim: The Book of the Union also reports a view of Henana's: 'D'après letraité De Unione, Henana admettait que le corps du Christ ressuscité et ceux des fidèles ... étaient [sphériques] (ms., p. 126)' (Greek word garbled in OCR)
claims.witness: Labourt's note (labourt1904 l.15816-15818); the Chronicle of Seert lists Babai's book 'contre coux qui disent que les corps au jour de la resurrection ressusciteront dans la forme d'une sphere' (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29684-29686)

claims.claim: Labourt: 'les écrits de l'archimandrite d'Izla contribuèrent par leur large diffusion au triomphe de la dogmatique officielle'
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.13097-13099)

claims.claim: After Khosrau's murder 'all the fathers entreated the holy Mar Bibhai to be Catholicus; but he would not accept the office at all'; the angel 'in the form of a horseman holding a fiery sword'; 'As long as thou wast the vicar of the Catholicus, from the first day even until now, I never departed from thy side'; 'If I had known that thou wast with me, I would, with all care, have accepted this great work; but now depart in peace, and pray for me;' (the brief closes the quotation with a full stop for the file's semicolon)
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors I.35 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.5164-5188)

claims.claim: Labourt: the offer 'ne lui fut faite que pour la forme'
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.13534-13535)

claims.claim: Scher: 'Seloa Thomas de Marga, Babai est mort apres Kosrau, mort en 628; selon notre auteur, il preceda dans la tombe le roi Kosrau. II serait ne en 552/3 et aurait succcde a Dadis6' en 603/4'
claims.witness: Scher's note to the Chronicle of Seert (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29693-29695)

claims.claim: Budge: 'Babhai the Great, third governor of the Monastery of Izla, flourished about A. D. 569 — 628'; Khosrau II murdered in 628
claims.witness: Budge's note (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.2067-2081)

claims.claim: Works: Thomas, 'eighty and four of his works on various subjects are preserved, and are held in honour by the holy Church'; Abdisho, 'Babai the Great wrote eighty-three books'; the Chronicle of Seert lists 'Livre de runion' and a book explaining 'en abrege, les paroles de Mar Evagrius'; Scher: the Book of the Union 'nous est parvenu dans un manuscrit'; the Evagrius work 'est conserve dans un manuscrit a la bibliotheque Vaticane'
claims.witness: Thomas I.28 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.4189-4191); Badger's English of Abdisho (badger v2 l.17741); Chronicle of Seert and Scher's notes (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29714, 29719-29720, 29726-29728, 29731)

claims.claim: George: born Mihramgouënasp, of a noble family, converted from Magism, monk in Dadisho's convent on Izla; 'MASSACRE PAR KoSRAU' (chapter title); Scher: the Life 'a ete publiee par Bedjan'
claims.witness: Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42083-42088); Chronicle of Seert LXXXVI title and Scher's note (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.29868, 29875-29877)

claims.claim: Ishoyahb, writing as bishop (heading 'EPISTULAE Ali Isf/VAHB SCRIPTAE CUM EPISCOPUS ESSET', OCR for AB ISO'YAHB), to 'Sanctissimo Patri nostro benedicto Mar Babai': 'Huiusmodi enim periculum procellarum barbararum cum vicis- set sollicitudo zeli tui per multos annos, o Pater sanctissime'; and to the brothers on Mount Izla on the death of their superior: 'hunc ducem magnum et illustrissimum in numerum sanctorum rettulistis' ... 'beatus et sanctissimus Pater noster benedictus Mar Babai' (the printer's line number 'a5' between 'sanctissimus' and 'Pater' omitted)
claims.witness: Ishoyahb III, Letters II and XI, tr. Duval (ishoyahb-iii liber-epistularum duval1905 l.339, 378-379, 403-405, 733, 766-777); a contemporary, admiring witness; OCR heading garbled

claims.claim: Wigram: 'Babai, though not a bishop, acted as patriarch in all ecclesiastical matters as far as authority went'
claims.witness: Wigram (wigram 1910 l.12219-12221)

claims.claim: Labourt: Dadisho 'mourut âgé de soixante-quinze ans, ... entre 615 et 620'
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.17771-17772)

claims.claim: Book III, chapters I-III of Thomas (schools, books, death of 'Rabban Babhai') concern another man: 'He came from a family in the town of Gebhilta'; 'the period in which he lived was in the days of Selibha-zekha, Catholicus'
claims.witness: Thomas, Book of Governors III.1 (thomas-of-marga book-of-governors-v2 budge1893 l.12888-12894)

contested_claims.claim: When Babai died, and whether he outlived Khosrau
contested_claims.sides: Chronicle of Seert: died at 75 in Khosrau's 38th year (seert l.29679-29680), which Scher reads as before the king, with a birth in 552/3 (l.29693-29695). Thomas of Marga: alive after Khosrau's murder, refused the catholicate (budge1893 l.5164-5167); Budge: flourished to 628 (l.2067-2068). Ishoyahb's letter on his death gives no year (duval1905 l.733-777).

contested_claims.claim: What Henana taught, as Babai reports it
contested_claims.sides: Babai, in the Life of George and the Book of the Union (chabot1902 l.42093-42112; labourt1904 l.15816-15818), and the Chronicle of Seert's list of his anti-Henana work (seert l.29560-29561). Braun calls Babai passionate and corrects for his exaggerations (braun1900 l.13690-13696); see henana-of-adiabene, batch 5.

contested_claims.claim: Whether the offer of the catholicate was real
contested_claims.sides: Thomas tells it as earnest (budge1893 l.5164-5167); Labourt thinks it was made only for form (labourt1904 l.13534-13535).
Scher, from the Chronicle of Seert's 24 years: 603/4 (seert l.29695); Labourt puts Dadisho's death between 615 and 620 (labourt1904 l.17771-17772).

absent_details.detail: A Syriac or English text of his own books
absent_details.note: The Book of the Union is held only as passages quoted in Labourt's French (l.15845-16120); the Life of George only as two passages in Chabot's French (l.42081-42240). Searched all of cic/texts for Babai/Babaï/Babhai/Babaeus.
No held ancient line. 552/3 is Scher's reckoning; Budge gives fl. 569-628.

absent_details.detail: Mari and Amr on Babai the Great
absent_details.note: Gismondi's Latin Mari and Amr, as OCR'd, name other Babais (the catholicos, Babai of Kashkar, Babai of Nisibis) but no line naming Babai the Great was found; Scher cites Mari p. 61 and Amr p. 52 (seert l.29692).

absent_details.detail: The scan row's Book III lead
absent_details.note: Thomas Book III ch. I-III (l.12841-13575) is Rabban Babai of Gebilta under Selibha-zekha, not Babai the Great.

claims.claim: 'On the fifth of January he began to be slightly dis- quieted by a pain in the side. When this persisted for three days, at midnight he commanded the breth- ren to be with him'; 'altogether forbade that they should weep for him. Having stretched out his hand, and made the sign of the cross over his whole body, he commanded that they should sing a psalm. When the grief that overspread them kept them silent, he himself started the psalm, " Praise ye the Lord in his sanctuary; let everything that hath breath praise the Lord." And so, on the eighth of January, repeating this verse, while we could hardly make the responses, he fell asleep in the Lord.'
claims.witness: Eugippius, Life of Severinus XLII-XLIII, tr. Robinson (eugippius robinson1914 l.3709-3712, 3828-3837); hagiography by a member of his community

claims.claim: Eugippius prepared 'a memoir, filled full with testimonies from the daily narrations of the elder brethren'; 'Even in the lifetime of Saint Severinus, I never heard other particulars in regard to his native place'; he writes as one of the community ('our elders', 'us who stood by')
claims.witness: Eugippius, letter to Paschasius and XLIII-XLIV (eugippius robinson1914 l.294-296, 477-479, 3839, 3960-3962)

claims.claim: The letter was written about two years after 'the consulship of Impor- tunus', which Robinson dates 'A.D. 509'
claims.witness: Eugippius and Robinson's note (eugippius robinson1914 l.278-279, 301)

claims.claim: 'At the time of the death of Attila, king of the Huns, ... Severinus, most holy servant of God, came from the parts of the East to the marches of Riverside Noricum and the Pan- nonias, and tarried in a little town which is called Asturis'; Robinson: 'In 453'
claims.witness: Eugippius I (eugippius robinson1914 l.788-793); Robinson's note (l.804)

claims.claim: Primenius's question and the answer: 'What profiteth it the servant of God to name his country or race, when by keeping them silent he can more easily avoid vainglory ?'; 'Yet his speech revealed a man of purest Latin stock; and it is understood that he first departed into some desert place of the East'; the towns 'were harassed by frequent incursions of the barbarians'
claims.witness: Eugippius, letter to Paschasius (eugippius robinson1914 l.395-452)

claims.claim: He urged Comagenis 'to be armed with fasting and prayers and almsgivings'; great numbers 'faithfully gave the poor the tithes of their crops'; the table of chapters: 'the Norici also were wont to send tithes to him for distribution'; 'He was asked to accept the honorable office of bishop. But he closed the matter with a determined refusal'
claims.witness: Eugippius I, XVII, IX (eugippius robinson1914 l.864-865, 2279-2281 and the chapter table l.602-603, 1689-1691)

claims.claim: Odoacer, 'then a tall youth, meanly clad'; '" Go forth! " said Severinus, " Go forth to Italy! Now clad in wretched hides, thou shalt soon distribute rich gifts to many."'
claims.witness: Eugippius VII (eugippius robinson1914 l.1489-1523)

claims.claim: Giso 'even attemp- ted to rebaptize certain Catholics. But when her husband, out of his reverence for Saint Severinus, did not consent, she incontinently abandoned her sacri- legious purpose'
claims.witness: Eugippius VIII (eugippius robinson1914 l.1531-1538)

claims.claim: To Flaccitheus: 'If the one Catholic faith united us, thou oughtest rather to con- sult me concerning eternal life'; Robinson concludes the Rugian sovereigns were 'Christians of the Arian sect'; Adlzreitter: 'sacrilego Arianorum fonte denuo lustrare'
claims.witness: Eugippius V and Robinson's notes (eugippius robinson1914 l.1297-1310, 1550-1552)

claims.claim: 'God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones from hence'; Onoulfus 'or- dered all the Romans to migrate to Italy'; at the opening of the grave 'the sixth year of his burial had already passed'; the body was carried to Mount Feleter; then, 'with the authorization of Saint Gelasius, pontiff of the Roman see, and received by the people of Naples ... the body was laid to rest by the hands of Saint Victor the bishop in the Lucullan castle, in a mausoleum which Bar- baria had built'
claims.witness: Eugippius XL, XLIV, XLVI (eugippius robinson1914 l.3583-3585, 3927-3928, 3964-3966, 4037-4049)

claims.claim: Robinson: 'c. 482, 8 Jan. Death of Severinus at his monastery near Favianis (43)'; '487. Odoacer wages war on the Rugii'
claims.witness: Robinson's chronological table (eugippius robinson1914 l.4863-4866)

claims.claim: Foulke's note: 'He died A. D. 482, and his body was taken to Italy and finally buried at Naples (Waitz)'; 'He was born either in Southern Italy or in Africa'
claims.witness: Paul the Deacon, History of the Langobards I.19, note (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.2672-2677)

claims.claim: Paul: 'In these territories of the Noricans at that time was the monastery of the blessed Severinus'; he admonished Feletheus and 'his wife, whose name was Gisa'; 'Neapolis (Naples) keeps his remains'; Foulke: Paul 'amplifies with additions from Eugippius Life of St. Severinus'
claims.witness: Paul the Deacon I.19, tr. Foulke (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.2649-2659, 14530-14531)

claims.claim: Paschasius: 'I have thought it best not to try to make any addition to thy work'; 'The virtues of teachers are particularly visible in their daily life, and consequently are more easily depicted by their pupils.'
claims.witness: Letter of Paschasius to Eugippius (eugippius robinson1914 l.4253-4260)

claims.claim: Title-page epigraph: 'Severin: eine Personlichkeit, zu der es keine Parallele giebt.' Hauck, Kirchengeschichte Deutschlands (OCR 'Personlichkeit')
claims.witness: eugippius robinson1914 l.65-67

claims.claim: Robinson's note on Willibald, 'the Saxon pilgrim, who visited Naples in 729. " Et ibi est prope castella [sic] ubi requiescit sanctus Severinus."'
claims.witness: Robinson's preface note (eugippius robinson1914 l.167-170)

claims.claim: Robinson on Sommerlad's account of his early life: it 'needs mention only by way of caution'
claims.witness: Robinson's note (eugippius robinson1914 l.465, 487)

claims.claim: Gregory the Great to Anthemius, subdeacon of Campania: the people of Sorrento 'Amandum presbyterum oratorii fan- &i Severini quod in caftro Lucullano fitum eft , elegerunt' (OCR long s as f, '&' for ct)
claims.witness: Gregory the Great, letter, in Mansi 10 (mansi tomus-10 welter1901 l.23210-23229); attests the oratory, not the life

claims.claim: He lived near Favianis: 'Near this town, as I have related, Saint Severinus dwelt'
claims.witness: Eugippius XLII (eugippius robinson1914 l.3663-3667)

contested_claims.sides: Eugippius gives only 8 January (l.3835). Robinson: c. 482 (l.4863); Foulke's note, after Waitz: 482 (foulke1907 l.2674). Both are reckonings; no source gives a year.

Eugippius: unknown, of purest Latin stock by his speech, first in an Eastern desert (l.395-452). Foulke's note, after Waitz: Southern Italy or Africa (foulke1907 l.2672-2673). Robinson cautions against Sommerlad's detailed account.

absent_details.detail: A second independent witness to his life
absent_details.note: None held. Paul the Deacon (foulke1907 l.2649-2659) draws on Eugippius (Foulke l.14530-14531). Whole-Library search for Severin* beside Noric-/Eugipp-/Favian-/Lucull-/Odoac- finds only citations and, in Mansi 10, Gregory the Great's letter naming his oratory in the Lucullan castle (l.23224-23229) (Mansi 7, Acta Sanctorum, MGH SRM 2 and 3, Duchesne's Liber Pontificalis note, PL 67 and 88).

absent_details.detail: Words of his own in writing
absent_details.note: None. His sayings come through Eugippius.

absent_details.detail: His age, family and the year he came to Noricum
absent_details.note: Eugippius gives none; 453 is Robinson's year for Attila's death.
